title: Quantifying the effects of data augmentation and stain color normalization in convolutional neural networks for computational pathology
study_context: Cross-laboratory study of stain variation mitigation in computational pathology.
population_or_data: H&E images from four organs and nine pathology laboratories.
task: Quantify how augmentation and stain normalization affect CNN generalization.
method: Experimental comparison of stain color augmentation and normalization techniques.
main_findings: Stain variation across laboratories can degrade CNN transfer, and augmentation or normalization can reduce generalization error depending on the setup.
limitations: The experiments use H&E patch/CNN tasks and do not evaluate this project's event-level multi-stain branch design.
does_not_establish: The paper does not justify a single universally optimal stain-normalization pipeline for all stains and encoders.
relevance_to_project: Evidence for treating stain/site shift as an empirical robustness question with explicit ablation.
